commit_message: feat: load config from APP_* environment variables
summary: Config loader whose tests guard every assertion behind `if (result.ok)` / `if (!result.ok)`, and whose no-warning test spies on console.error while warnings go to console.warn.

defects.description: Every loadConfig test asserts only inside `if (result.ok)` or `if (!result.ok)` with no expect.assertions / no assertion on `ok`, so a test passes when the result has the other shape: e.g. if the port validation always fails, `uses defaults` and `reads overrides` still pass; if it never fails, `rejects an invalid port` still passes. Mutants such as the port check -> `false` survive. Tests should assert `result` with toEqual({ ok: true, config: ... }) / toEqual({ ok: false, error: ... }).

`does not warn about known settings` spies on `console.error`, but warn() writes to `console.warn` (and log.warnings), so `expect(spy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` is vacuous: it passes even when known settings do warn, and there is no positive control showing the spy sees a warning for an unknown APP_* key. Spy on the real channel (or assert log.warnings) and add a positive case.

Only 70000 is tested as invalid; the boundaries 0/1 and 65535/65536, non-integers ("80.5"), and non-numbers are untested, so `port < 1` -> `<= 1`, `port > 65535` -> `>=`, and the isInteger check survive. The host override is never asserted either.
